findings.claim: Bulk purge (purge_all_trash, purge_all_missing) calls physical_delete, which now raises 409 for an ambiguous name after earlier files in the same loop were already unlinked and before the single commit.
findings.impact: One ambiguous entry aborts the batch. Files processed earlier are gone from disk while their rows stay in Trash or Missing until a second purge. A second purge succeeds because the unlink is skipped for an absent file. The main.py trash purge job commits per row, so it is not affected.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/fileops.py physical_delete (existing_or_409 then unlink); purge_all_trash loop commits once after the loop; backend/app/main.py:96 commits per row.

bucket_proposal.reason: I12 requires 409 and no change for the ambiguous file itself. It does not cover a batch partial state. Recoverable by repeating the purge.

findings.proposed_fix: Commit per row in the bulk purges, or skip and report an ambiguous file.

findings.claim: The commit adds no parity-table JSON fixture, and the core resolver has no table-driven test.
findings.impact: I16 cannot be checked for the core copy; the touch-point list requires the table in each tree that holds a resolver.
findings.evidence: Glob for parity files finds only older unrelated parity tests; no fixture for the resolver exists.

bucket_proposal.reason: I16 states every resolver copy returns the table's results; with no table the invariant is unchecked in core.

findings.proposed_fix: Add the JSON fixture and a test that runs the core resolver against it, or state that it ships with the addon PR.

findings.claim: Many handlers were moved to asyncio.to_thread and start_import was split into prepare_import and launch_import. These routers (admin_markdown_images, uploads) and handlers are not in the touch-point list.
findings.impact: Scope and concurrency change beyond path resolution. The request Session and the module globals _jobs and _current_job_id are used on worker threads. The calls are sequential per request, so I found no concrete race.

bucket_proposal.reason: No declared invariant is broken. Section 10 motivates the threading, but the touch-point list omits these files.

findings.proposed_fix: List these files and handlers in the touch points.

findings.claim: complete_upload resolves the leaf non-strictly, so a twin of the target that appeared after init_upload is replaced in place.
findings.impact: Rare race. It matches the in-place replacement of spec step 6. No test covers the complete step.

bucket_proposal.reason: Likely the intended behavior; only the test is missing.

specification_compliance: I1 to I12: reads go through _on_disk_path or resolve_on_disk(cached=True). Mutators use existing_or_409 and new_or_409 without the cache. The walk checks the exact name first, treats dot and empty components as matching nothing, and writes nothing.
I13: the AST inventory test exists with a seeded-detector self-check and an empty LISTING_DERIVED.
I16: no core parity fixture found.
I14 and I15: addon work, outside this commit.
potential_unspecified_behavior: start_import split into prepare_import and launch_import.
regression_risks: Mutators refuse an ambiguous pair while readers pick the first by sorted bytes.
An extra lexists and a scandir on a miss on hot read paths.
test_coverage: Good coverage of I1 to I12 through the leaf, ancestor and both layouts, with ambiguity 409, batch rollback, scan stability and symlink cases.
No test covers a bulk purge that hits an ambiguous entry, complete_upload resolution, or the thread offloading.
not_verified: I ran no tests; the tools are read-only.
I did not read the full fileops mutator bodies.
I did not inspect the addons.
I did not verify SQLAlchemy Session thread-safety.
trajectory: There are no fix commits since r1; the only commit after r1 records the review. No round added or removed a branch, state or prediction, so I see no sign the design is being patched.
